evals.prompt: what data do we have available to query?
evals.expected_output: An inventory-style response listing raw/normalized per-venue exchange files, instrument metadata and the current partitioned Paradigm execution tape under s3://dt-exchange-venue-data; the Paradigm RFQ and legacy historical executed CSV tapes under s3://dt-paradigm-data/paradigm_data/; and the Paradex DEX trade tape under s3://dt-paradex-data/paradex_data/. Mentions ap-northeast-1 and credential-chain access. Does not use the hot prefix.
assertions: Response names the S3 buckets (s3://dt-paradigm-data, s3://dt-exchange-venue-data, s3://dt-paradex-data)
Response lists raw exchange venue files and metadata, the current partitioned Paradigm execution tape, Paradigm RFQ and legacy executed CSV tapes, and the Paradex DEX trade tape
Response does not recommend s3://dt-exchange-venue-data/hot/ or any hot__ object
Response is structured as a catalog summary, not a query — it does not attempt to run SQL

evals.prompt: do we have OKX combo quotes?
evals.expected_output: A direct answer: there is no dedicated OKX combo-quote feed. Points to raw OKX option_trade and option_summary partitions as the available leg-level trade/quote evidence, explains that block_trade_id can group real block legs, and does not fabricate a path or recommend hot files.
assertions: Response clearly states there is no dedicated OKX combo-quote feed
Response points to raw OKX option_trade and/or option_summary data as what is available
Response does not fabricate an S3 path (no external/tardis, no terminal-dime-prod)

evals.prompt: what columns does the Paradigm trade tape have and where does it live?
evals.expected_output: Response leads with current daily Parquet at s3://dt-exchange-venue-data/paradigm_trade_tape/year=YYYY/month=MM/day=DD/paradigm_trade_tape__YYYYMMDD.parquet, lists its lowercase leg-level columns, and gives the case-sensitive options filter instrument_kind == "OPTION". It distinguishes the legacy s3://dt-paradigm-data/paradigm_data/paradigm_trade_tape_slim.csv.gz frozen at 2026-08-10, whose uppercase columns are not the Parquet schema. Current objects are mutable, support trailing 30-day reads plus the full oldest UTC day, and require metadata freshness/coverage checks.
assertions: Response identifies the current tape at s3://dt-exchange-venue-data/paradigm_trade_tape/ with year/month/day partitions and paradigm_trade_tape__YYYYMMDD.parquet filenames
Response lists current Parquet columns including traded_at, trade_id, rfq_id, block_trade_id, venue_block_trade_id, instrument_kind, trade_price, notional_volume_usd
Response gives the case-sensitive options-only filter instrument_kind == "OPTION" (or equivalent SQL equality with uppercase OPTION), not merely the legacy PRODUCT filter
Response distinguishes current partitioned Parquet from the legacy paradigm_trade_tape_slim.csv.gz frozen at 2026-08-10, without presenting the frozen CSV as the only execution dataset
Response explains bounded recent coverage and checking freshness or coverage metadata rather than treating all historical days as available

evals.prompt: what's the latest Deribit option trade data available?
evals.expected_output: A helpful answer pointing to the raw Deribit option_trade and option_summary partitions under s3://dt-exchange-venue-data/raw/exchange=deribit/, with dvol and perp_summary as related raw feeds. Explains the partition layout and recommends checking max(timestamp) in the narrow latest partition. Does not cite hot, terminal-dime-prod, or external/tardis paths.
assertions: Response points to raw Deribit option_trade and option_summary paths under s3://dt-exchange-venue-data/raw/
Response does not cite a terminal-dime-prod or external/tardis S3 path
Response recommends checking record timestamps in a narrow raw partition rather than assuming coverage
